doc.title: Mickey Roker interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

chapter: Roots in the church and Africa
title: African drums as communication
summary: Drums sent messages by tone, which is why slave owners took them away.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: You also talked about the drums in West African society being a form of communication and that was a form of using significant tones.

That’s how they speak to each other. Whatever tone. You know they had kinds of sounds for different messages that they wanted to send. And not only the sound but the way the sound was projected, you know, tells a story. But you have to live, like again like I say, you have to live in order to understand these sounds. There’s no way that somebody that don’t live there can tell you what these guys are saying. You know what they’re doing, they’re sending messages, which you don’t know what the messages, see that’s what made ‘em take the drums away. Because they didn’t know. They couldn’t understand what these slaves were saying. So they just took the drums, you know, I mean after they come to America, and so that’s how—
